reply.overview: This five-color Avatar-themed deck uses [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] to turn every bending trigger into a card and eventually flip into a creature that reduces spell costs and drains opponents on each upkeep. Lesson spells, Shrines, and Ally synergies flood the board with tokens and earthbent lands while [[Aang, the Last Airbender]], [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]], and [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] can combine to make infinite creature tokens and ETB/LTB triggers once assembled.

strategy: Ramp early with artifacts and creatures like [[Sol Ring]] and [[Hermitic Herbalist]] to cast [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] around turn 3.
Trigger waterbend, earthbend, firebend, and airbend effects each turn to draw cards and flip [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]].
Build board presence with Allies and Shrines like [[Southern Air Temple]] and [[Crescent Island Temple]] for wide attacks.
Assemble [[Aang, the Last Airbender]], [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]], and [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] for infinite creature tokens and triggers.
Close games with flipped [[Aang, Master of Elements]] dealing repeated damage and drawing extra cards each upkeep.

keep: A hand with early ramp like [[Arcane Signet]] or [[Sol Ring]] into a turn four commander.
A hand with a Lesson spell and a way to bend an element for card draw.
sendBack: A hand with no path to cast [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] by turn 4.
A hand full of high-cost spells and no early mana sources.

cards: Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements
tips.text: Together these three make infinite creature ETB and LTB triggers once assembled with only 1 mana needed to run.
[[Gran-Gran]] draws and discards while [[Toph, Hardheaded Teacher]] returns discarded instants or sorceries from the graveyard.
[[Jeong Jeong, the Deserter]] can copy [[Elemental Teachings]] when cast as a Lesson spell for extra land fetching.
[[Katara, the Fearless]] doubles the Ally token trigger from [[Katara, Water Tribe's Hope]] entering the battlefield.

No mass removal means it struggles against wide opposing boards.
The infinite combo pieces are spread across three specific cards that may not come together.

reply.overview: Kilo, Apogee Mind leads a Jeskai artifact counters deck that builds toward infinite proliferate and locked-up extra turns. Kilo himself triggers proliferate whenever he taps, feeding a wide artifact base of counter synergies and ramp. Alongside the counter theme, the deck assembles Basalt Monolith and Zirda, the Dawnwaker for infinite colorless mana, Unctus, Grand Metatect with Pemmin's Aura or Freed from the Real for infinite looting, Kilo, Apogee Mind with Pemmin's Aura and Relic of Legends for infinite proliferate, and Inspirit, Flagship Vessel with Kilo, Apogee Mind and Magistrate's Scepter for infinite turns.

strategy: Ramp early with artifact mana rocks and land fixing to cast Kilo, Apogee Mind around turn 3.
Tap Kilo, Apogee Mind repeatedly to proliferate counters across artifacts, creatures and planeswalkers.
Assemble Basalt Monolith with Zirda, the Dawnwaker for infinite colorless mana to fund other abilities.
Chain Inspirit, Flagship Vessel with Kilo, Apogee Mind and Magistrate's Scepter into infinite turns.
Use Unctus, Grand Metatect with Pemmin's Aura or Freed from the Real to loot through the deck infinitely.

keep: A hand with early ramp like Arcane Signet into a turn to cast [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]].
Any hand with [[Sol Ring]] and a follow-up spell to use the mana on.
sendBack: A hand full of high-cost artifacts with no early plays before turn 3.
A hand missing any way to proliferate or support [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]]'s ability.

tips.text: Pemmin's Aura taps and untaps Kilo, Apogee Mind, triggering repeated proliferate while Relic of Legends refunds the mana.
Zirda, the Dawnwaker lowers the untap cost on Basalt Monolith enough to generate infinite colorless mana.
Station counters from Inspirit, Flagship Vessel help power Magistrate's Scepter into locking opponents out with extra turns.
Freed from the Real lets Unctus, Grand Metatect tap and untap itself, looting repeatedly under its own draw-discard ability.

Stations counters to fuel extra-turn engine.1

Draws cards and cheapens artifact activations.1
Turns tapped artifacts into damage and scry.1

weaknesses: Many combo pieces need to be assembled together, so hands can stall without one piece.
The deck has only 6 interaction cards and no mass removal to catch up from behind.
Heavy reliance on artifacts makes it vulnerable to decks that punish artifact-heavy boards.

reply.overview: This Colorless deck builds a ramp-heavy artifact and Eldrazi shell that casts huge colorless spells to chain cascades off [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]]. Mana rocks and Eldrazi lands push toward big threats like [[Artisan of Kozilek]] and [[Kozilek, the Great Distortion]], while [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Forsaken Monument]] can generate infinite colorless mana. Board wipes like [[All Is Dust]] and [[Ugin, the Spirit Dragon]] clear the way for the deck's Eldrazi and Construct tokens to close out games.

strategy: Ramp early with rocks like [[Sol Ring]] and [[Thran Dynamo]] to reach big mana fast.
Cast [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] around turn 5 to enable double cascade on huge spells.
Deploy colossal Eldrazi threats such as [[Kozilek, the Great Distortion]] and [[It That Betrays]] off cascades.
Assemble [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Forsaken Monument]] for infinite colorless mana to fuel the rest of the deck.
Clear boards with [[All Is Dust]] or [[Ugin, the Spirit Dragon]] before swinging with surviving threats.

keep: A hand with early ramp like [[Mind Stone]] leading into bigger spells.
A hand with [[Sol Ring]] plus a plan to keep casting things after it.
sendBack: A hand full of expensive spells with no ramp to reach them.
A hand with [[Sol Ring]] but nothing to cast after it stalls out.

tips.text: [[Basalt Monolith]] untaps itself endlessly once [[Forsaken Monument]] doubles its colorless output.
Casting [[Artisan of Kozilek]] off [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]]'s cascade can return a creature from the graveyard immediately.
[[Ugin's Mastery]] manifests cards whenever you cast colorless creatures, which also pumps [[Skittering Cicada]] in combat.
[[Mystic Forge]] lets you cast [[Treasure Map]] straight off the top of your library.

Doubles colorless mana and pumps colorless creatures.
Refills hand and counters spells via discard.

Cheap finisher that recurs itself from the graveyard.

weaknesses: Relies on reaching high mana values, so early disruption to ramp can stall the whole plan.
Interaction is limited at instant speed, leaving some turns where opponents act unchecked.
Color identity restricts the deck to colorless answers, which can miss specific threats.

reply.overview: This Naya Dinosaur tribal deck builds toward casting [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] around turn 7 and swinging to cheat more Dinosaurs onto the battlefield off the top of the library. Cost reducers and ramp get big threats out early, while [[Polyraptor]] combos with [[Forerunner of the Empire]] or [[Marauding Raptor]] to flood the board with tokens or end the game outright.

strategy: Ramp through dinosaur-cost reducers and mana rocks toward [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]].
Cast [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] and attack to cheat Dinosaurs onto the battlefield.
Assemble [[Forerunner of the Empire]] with [[Polyraptor]], or [[Marauding Raptor]] with [[Polyraptor]], for endless tokens.
Use enrage triggers from creatures like [[Ripjaw Raptor]] and [[Trapjaw Tyrant]] to grind out value.
Close games with trampling attackers like [[Ghalta, Primal Hunger]] or [[The Tarrasque]].

keep: A hand with early cost reducers like [[Otepec Huntmaster]] or [[Knight of the Stampede]].
A hand with [[Sol Ring]] or another early ramp piece plus a follow-up play.

reply.overview: This mono-Red Goblin tribal deck builds toward [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] flooding the board with tokens, then converting that army into damage through anthems, sacrifice outlets, and direct burn. With [[Goblin Warchief]] or [[Goblin Chieftain]] alongside [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] and [[Skirk Prospector]], the deck can assemble infinite commander casts and infinite hasty Goblin tokens. Smaller burn spells and removal clear blockers while the Goblins swing or get sacrificed for value and damage.

strategy: Ramp early with artifacts and Goblin mana dorks to reach [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] around turn 4.
Activate [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] to flood the board with Goblin tokens each turn it survives.
Assemble [[Goblin Warchief]] or [[Goblin Chieftain]] with [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] and [[Skirk Prospector]] for infinite hasty tokens and casts.
Use burn spells and sacrifice outlets like [[Goblin Bombardment]] and [[Tar Pitcher]] to close out the game.
Clear key blockers with removal like [[Lightning Bolt]] and [[Abrade]] before attacking.

keep: A hand with an early mana rock like [[Sol Ring]] or [[Arcane Signet]] leading into turns 2-4.
A hand with [[Goblin Matron]] or [[Dragon Fodder]] to build the board before [[Krenko, Mob Boss]].
sendBack: A hand reliant only on late high-cost burn with no early plays.
A hand where [[Sol Ring]] has nothing to cast after it stalls out.

tips.text: With [[Goblin Warchief]] and [[Skirk Prospector]] out, [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] can loop into infinite hasty Goblin tokens.
[[Goblin Chieftain]] grants the haste needed so [[Skirk Prospector]] and [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] can go infinite together.
Casting [[Firebolt]] and later its flashback both trigger [[Guttersnipe]] for extra damage to opponents.
[[Mogg War Marshal]] leaves a token behind when sacrificed to [[Goblin Bombardment]] for extra value.

Finds any Goblin card needed from the library.
Grinds down every player's life each upkeep.

weaknesses: The deck has no mass removal, so it can struggle against a wide opposing board.
Krenko, Mob Boss dying or being removed repeatedly slows the whole plan considerably.
The deck leans heavily on token generation, making it vulnerable to one-sided wraths from opponents.

reply.overview: This Jeskai deck leans on the god tribal theme and counter synergies, building experience counters and proliferate effects to grow creatures huge while [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] and [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] generate value from Gods dying and attacking. The deck wins through accumulating +1/+1 counters, overwhelming boards with devotion-based Gods, and burst damage from triggered abilities like [[Purphoros, God of the Forge]] and [[Toralf, God of Fury // Toralf's Hammer]], finishing with wide combat damage or direct burn.

strategy: Ramp early with artifacts and lands into your Gods and commanders around turn 4.
Attack with Gods to generate experience counters via [[Kratos, Stoic Father]].
Use proliferate effects to grow counters across the board quickly.
Leverage [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] to refill your hand and burn opponents using stored experience counters.
Close games with wide attacks backed by indestructible or protection effects like [[Akroma's Will]] or [[Flawless Maneuver]].

A hand that curves into [[Smothering Tithe]] or [[Knight of the White Orchid]] for lands.

A hand missing both colored sources and ramp pieces.

tips.text: Casting any noncreature spell proliferates twice, growing counters on Gods and planeswalkers quickly.
Proliferate effects double thanks to [[Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus]], accelerating counter growth from cards like [[Contentious Plan]].

reply.overview: Baral, Chief of Compliance leads a mono-Blue Wizards deck built around cheap instants and sorceries, countering opposing spells, and drawing extra cards off that interaction. The deck can assemble infinite value loops using [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] with [[Sublime Epiphany]] or [[Ghostly Flicker]], generating infinite ETB and LTB triggers to overwhelm the table, while otherwise grinding opponents out with card advantage and countermagic.

strategy: Cast [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] around turn 2 to cheapen your spells.
Deploy cheap draw spells and Wizards to build card advantage.
Hold up countermagic like [[Counterspell]] and [[Mana Leak]] to protect your board.
Assemble [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] with [[Sublime Epiphany]] for infinite triggers.
Alternatively combo [[Ghostly Flicker]] with [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] for infinite loops.

keep: A hand with [[Preordain]] or [[Ponder]] to dig for [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]].
Early mana rocks like [[Mind Stone]] leading into counterspells.
sendBack: A hand full of countermagic but no way to draw into threats or lands.

Flickering Naru Meha with Ghostly Flicker loops infinite artifact and creature ETB and LTB triggers.

reply.overview: This Dimir deck builds around [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]], using cheap unblockable creatures and ninjutsu to sneak Ninjas in, triggering Yuriko's ability to reveal cards and drain life equal to their mana value. Counterspells and removal protect the attack while extra-turn spells and card selection push damage through quickly for a direct life-total finish.

strategy: Play unblockable evasive creatures like [[Slither Blade]] or [[Tormented Soul]] early.
Ninjutsu them out for [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] or other Ninjas to trigger damage.
Chain combat damage triggers from Ninjas like [[Ingenious Infiltrator]] and [[Ninja of the Deep Hours]] for card advantage.
Hold up counterspells such as [[Counterspell]] and [[Swan Song]] to protect your board.
Close games with extra turns from [[Temporal Mastery]] or [[Time Warp]] once the attack is rolling.

keep: An unblockable creature alongside early mana to ninjutsu in [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]].
A hand with interaction like [[Counterspell]] plus a way to develop lands.
sendBack: A hand full of high-cost spells with no early unblockable creature.
Hands relying only on [[Expropriate]] or other late-game payoffs with no early plan.

tips.text: [[Satoru Umezawa]] grants ninjutsu to every creature in hand, letting you stream Ninjas in alongside [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]].
Ninjutsu in [[Ink-Eyes, Servant of Oni]] after an unblocked hit to steal a creature from an opponent's graveyard while triggering [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]].
[[Silver-Fur Master]] cheapens ninjutsu costs and pumps [[Mist-Syndicate Naga]], which copies itself on damage for a growing Ninja army.
[[Bojuka Bog]] exiling a graveyard can shrink what [[Drown in the Loch]] is able to counter or destroy, so sequence carefully.
